subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — KiteBank POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kitebank.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@kitebank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — KiteBank POC

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and really appreciated the clarity on your fraud-detection use case. Per our call, attached is a short recap of the demo plus a proposed POC plan that outlines success criteria, the evaluation approach, timeline, and ownership. High-level summary below: 

- Success criteria (what would make this a win for KiteBank):
  - >90% recall on labeled fraud transactions in the pilot dataset
  - Average inference latency <= 300ms at 95th percentile for a 512-token real-time scoring path
  - Integration with your event stream for scoring within 24–48 hours of ingestion
  - No raw account data leaves KiteBank’s VPC during the POC (private connector + KMS)

- Proposed evaluation plan:
  1) Sandbox onboarding (data connectors + small sample dataset) — week 0–1
  2) Baseline run + metrics capture (compare current rules + model) — week 2
  3) Iteration (prompting/threshold tuning, light quantization for throughput) — week 3
  4) Final evaluation + handoff (SLO docs + runbook) — week 4

- Timeline & owners:
  - Kickoff: target Wed 19 May — Marissa (AM) to lead Redwood side, Camila will own infra/setup; Dylan is the technical escalation and will join architecture calls.
  - KiteBank owners: Aisha (product) and Tom (platform) for data access and acceptance testing.

- Next steps (requested):
  1) Confirm success criteria above and any additional acceptance checks by EOD Wed 12 May
  2) Approve POC timeline and confirm kickoff date
  3) Share a minimal pilot dataset or sample schema for the sandbox connector (S3 or secure share)

Attachment: Proposed_POC_Plan_KiteBank.pdf (1.2MB) — includes mutual action plan and checklist. Also linking the demo recording for internal reference.

If this looks good I’ll circulate a Mutual Action Plan (Excel) and create the initial HubSpot milestone.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — KiteBank POC

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap and for the plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the recall threshold is fine, but can we add a precision requirement for high-value transactions (> $10k) to avoid false positives impacting customers? Suggest precision >= 85% for that bucket.
- Data access: we cannot share raw account numbers. We can provide a de-identified sample or hashed IDs plus a mapping inside our secure sandbox. Can Redwood accept hashed identifiers and still compute accurate signals?
- Timeline: week-of-19 May kickoff works. Can we ask for an interim checkpoint at end of week 2 with preliminary metrics?

Also looping Tom on platform questions.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Product, Fraud Prevention | KiteBank
aisha.patel@kitebank.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kitebank.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@kitebank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — KiteBank POC

Hi Aisha / Tom — great notes, thanks.

Quoting your points and responding inline:

> - Add precision requirement for >$10k bucket (>=85%)
We can add that as an additional acceptance criterion. I’ll update the POC doc and the Mutual Action Plan.

> - Can Redwood accept hashed identifiers and still compute accurate signals?
Yes — our inference and feature extraction pipeline supports hashed IDs and tokenized identifiers. For the POC we typically work with hashed IDs + a small enrichment window (no raw PII leaves your environment). Camila will own the exact connector config; she can share the minimal schema we need.

> - Interim checkpoint at end of week 2
Absolutely — we’ll schedule a 30-minute checkpoint to share preliminary metrics and any blocker items.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Update Proposed_POC_Plan_KiteBank.pdf with the precision criterion and timeline adjustments (attached updated PDF).
- Create Mutual_Action_Plan_KiteBank.xlsx with owners, milestones, and acceptance criteria (attached).
- Create HubSpot milestone (HubSpot: 87654321) and send calendar invites for kickoff + interim checkpoint.

Proposed kickoff: Wed, 19 May at 10:30am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
